escalation.criterion: prompt Escalation Criteria rows 8 and 9 (negative and positive control failure)
escalation.observed: T0-T3 complete, dev tier (49/50 primary events). Negative control (placebo, no relationship to real data) produces separations up to 2258 bp, exceeding the smallest required threshold (133.9 bp) and the real iso_share result at 4 of 6 horizons. Positive control (133.9 bp planted) not cleanly recovered -- several horizons detect negative apparent separation. T4's original framing (compare against threshold) does not run: the comparison would report on data the controls have shown is not yet trustworthy at n=49. T4 was rescoped to a full-tier noise-band precheck (zero new tick reads, bootstrap over an already-committed full-universe artifact): the required separation clears the null's 5000-rep maximum by 12.7-19.2x its own std at every horizon, P(null>=required)=0/5000 everywhere -- the dev-tier failure was a sample-size problem, not a validity problem. T5 (full-tier ISO-share build) remains blocked on Cooper's explicit authorisation.

surprises: T2a: iso_share is not zero-inflated as expected going in (0% of 49 events at exactly zero)
T3: both the negative and positive controls fail on the first pass -- the raw uncontrolled real-iso_share separation (up to 795 bp) would have looked like a strong finding without them
T3b required a disclosed deviation from the prompt as written (planted-synthetic positive control instead of reusing candidate (a)'s print-level participation_rate, a grain mismatch)

T4 (added after review): the dev-tier control failure was a pure sample-size effect -- the same bootstrap at full tier clears the required separation by 12.7-19.2x, at zero read cost, before any full-tier ISO-share build was authorised

T4 also corrected an imprecise diagnosis in the original REPORT.md: the failure is bulk dispersion (IQR ~3100 bp) driving median standard error, not 'outlier events dominating the median' as first written -- a median is outlier-resistant by construction
